defect: File is not valid JSON: missing comma between the two HFC conditions
evidence: JSON.parse fails: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 159 column 23
impact_in_the_field: The app cannot parse the file at all - NO survey downloads or renders (all 3 surveys blocked by one comma)
suggested_fix: Add the comma; validate builder output with a JSON schema before publishing

defect: HFC conditions use the key "questioID" (typo) instead of "attr" - the key both reference specs use (Builder §11: attr = Core Attribute code or questionId; Android spec §3 example)
impact_in_the_field: The engine cannot find the question; the rule silently never fires (or crashes a strict parser)
suggested_fix: Rename the key to "attr"; the builder should generate keys from one model and the contract test rejects unknown keys

defect: HFC rule can never fire: it needs q_2 (slept well) = Yes but q_3 (hours) is only visible when q_2 = No
evidence: visibilityLogic: q_2 equals "No" ; rule: q_2 = "Yes" AND q_3 < 6
impact_in_the_field: The data-quality check the brief describes (sleeps well but < 6 h) is dead - bad data passes unchecked
suggested_fix: Decide intent: show q_3 for everyone (and drop "(If No)" from the label), or change the rule; builder should block contradictory rules

defect: No survey id
impact_in_the_field: Synced answers cannot be linked to the exact survey; renaming a title breaks reporting (Scenario A sync payload needs survey_id)
suggested_fix: Add a stable surveyId

defect: No schema version
impact_in_the_field: Old app versions in the field cannot tell which form version they hold; answers from v1 and v2 get mixed
suggested_fix: Add schemaVersion and send it with every synced record

defect: Numbers stored as strings ("min": "0", "max": "24", "val": "6")
impact_in_the_field: A parser comparing as text would flag 10 hours as < 6 or accept 30 hours
suggested_fix: Use JSON numbers

defect: validationRules is an object in some questions and an array in others
impact_in_the_field: Typed parsers (Kotlin/Moshi/Gson) may crash on one of the shapes
suggested_fix: Always an object (or always an array)

defect: Hint uses "questionHintText" while every other question uses "hintText"
impact_in_the_field: The app shows no hint for this question
suggested_fix: Use hintText everywhere

defect: "Other" option has no follow-up question to specify it
evidence: Survey 3 q_1 has one; Survey 1 q_2 does not
impact_in_the_field: Answer "Other" loses the real grade
suggested_fix: Add a q_2b specify question visible when q_2 = Other

defect: Section has no learningOutcome (all other sections do)
impact_in_the_field: Inconsistent section header in the app
suggested_fix: Make the field required in the builder or optional everywhere

defect: Every follow-up ("Why not?", "What games?", "How many hours?") has isRequired: false
evidence: isRequired false on q_4 / q_6 / q_3 ...
impact_in_the_field: When the follow-up appears it can be skipped - the reason data is often missing
suggested_fix: Required when visible (required + visibilityLogic)

defect: Labels contain logic notes for the enumerator, e.g. "(If Yes)", "(If No to breakfast)"
evidence: questionText: Why not? (If you said No)
impact_in_the_field: Shown to the respondent/enumerator on screen; wrong once logic changes (see PS-03); confusing after translation
suggested_fix: Move notes to checklistGuide; keep labels clean

defect: Message is unclear: "unusually low number of hours for sleeping standard"
impact_in_the_field: Low-literacy enumerators may not understand what to check
suggested_fix: Short, plain message: "Less than 6 hours sleep but said slept well. Please check."

defect: "reask_once", "severity": "Soft" and "show_sup": 1 ARE documented in Builder spec §11, but the brief (Scenario E) says "re-ask and flag", which is a different action (reask_and_flag: always flagged). With reask_once the answer is accepted after one re-ask and then flagged - the brief and the schema disagree on which one is wanted
impact_in_the_field: If the business expects every unusual answer to be confirmed and flagged, reask_once lets a second submit through after one re-ask
suggested_fix: Product owner to confirm reask_once vs reask_and_flag for this rule; show_sup (show to supervisor) meaning to be described in §11

defect: Options are plain display strings ("Yes", "By Doing") with no separate stored value
impact_in_the_field: No]
suggested_fix: Translating the label (e.g. to Hindi) breaks skip logic that compares with value Yes

defect: The HFC rule is stored under q_3 but depends on q_2
impact_in_the_field: If q_3 is removed or hidden the rule disappears or never runs
suggested_fix: Store cross-question checks at survey level

defect: No maximum length on free-text answers
impact_in_the_field: Very long text on 2G syncs slowly and can exceed server limits
suggested_fix: Add maxLength (e.g. 200)

defect: questionIds (q_1...) and sectionIds (sec_1...) repeat across surveys
impact_in_the_field: Fine only if every record also carries the survey id (blocked by PS-04)
suggested_fix: Keep ids unique per survey AND add surveyId

defect: No language field
evidence: Builder model §2: Form has language; surveyData has only title + sections
impact_in_the_field: Forms are produced per language; the app cannot tell which language version it received or sync it with the answers
suggested_fix: Add language (e.g. "en", "hi")

defect: Schema does not follow the Builder data model: sections hold "questions" (model: items[]); "sectionChecklist" string (model: checklistGuide[]); hintText and checklistGuide are strings (model: lists); "validationRules" {type,min,max} (model: validations[] of {type,value,message}); no hintMedia, trainingNote, isSensitive, isHidden ...
evidence: Builder spec §2, §5, §7 vs the provided file
impact_in_the_field: Either the builder exports a different format than it documents, or the app parses a format the builder will not produce - one of them breaks on the first real export
suggested_fix: Agree ONE contract (JSON Schema) shared by builder and app; contract tests on both sides

defect: The same rule id means two different things: Android spec §3 = q_3 > 16 ("unusually high"); provided schema = q_2 = Yes AND q_3 < 6 ("unusually low")
evidence: Android spec formChecks example vs schema survey 2 q_3
impact_in_the_field: Developers build/test against the spec example; the real rule (already unreachable, PS-03) is not what was tested
suggested_fix: Pick one meaning per id; give the "too high" and "too low" checks different ids

defect: Text says "Twenty input types are available" but the table lists 13
impact_in_the_field: Testers and developers cannot know whether 7 types are missing from the doc or the number is wrong; untested types may exist
suggested_fix: Correct the number or document the missing types

defect: The example rule has "op": " " (blank) - not one of the documented operators
impact_in_the_field: Anyone copying the example produces a rule that the app rejects or silently ignores
suggested_fix: Fix the example (e.g. "op": ">")
